title: Lineage IV foundational body plan
scope: Lineage-level body plan of Lineage IV, the fully aquatic flexible-trunk fin-fan lineage, distinguishing its ancestral core from the mass breeder's derived specialisations; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: Lineage IV is fully aquatic throughout; no branch is established as terrestrial or amphibious.
Its members occupy the full aquatic size and niche range, from small forms to the largest animals in their waters.

The lineage-wide inheritance is a locomotor and support core: a laterally flexible trunk carried on springy cartilage-analogue support, paired fin-fans as primary control surfaces, a muscular tail providing propulsion, and aquatic respiration through fold surfaces.

The mass breeder's exact three-pair fin-fan count, wedge-shaped mineralised head shield, dedicated ion-exchange organs, and wax-like-gel chambers are derived and branch-specific rather than lineage-wide.
The mass breeder is one specialised migratory member of the lineage, and its own records continue to govern it unchanged.
boundaries: Trunk, fin-fan, fold, and springy cartilage-analogue support are author-facing functional descriptions, not in-world names or formal taxonomy.
The plan establishes no fish, shark, cetacean, vertebrate, gill, fin-ray, or caudal-fin homology and no direct Earth-animal transplant.
Species, names, sizes, proportions, colours, lifespans, and the branch inventory remain open.

Fin-fan counts, positions, shapes, actuation, and specialisation outside the mass breeder's established three pairs remain open; paired establishes bilateral arrangement only, not any particular number.
Support-tissue composition, microstructure, stiffness, fatigue, and repair remain open, as do tail profile, gait, and swimming performance.
Respiratory-fold position, structure, ventilation, exchange capacity, and protective configurations remain open outside the mass breeder's case.

Which branches, if any, carry head shields, ion-exchange organs, or wax-like-gel chambers remains open; this record establishes none of them for any organism other than the mass breeder and adds nothing to the mass breeder's own physiology.

Fully aquatic throughout establishes no stranding tolerance, air breathing, amphibious capability, or overland movement, and no branch is established as unable to survive brief exposure; exposure limits remain open.
Occupying the full aquatic size and niche range is a radiation claim, not a dominance claim, and no particular aquatic niche is established as filled by this lineage at any place.
Reproduction across the lineage remains open; the mass breeder's mass egg deposition is its own established behaviour and is not lineage-wide.
Freshwater, brackish, and marine distribution, migration, salinity tolerance, senses, navigation, feeding, digestion, cognition, sociality, and disease remain open.

No Lineage IV branch other than the mass breeder is established as present, abundant, or absent at any particular location, including the basin lake, and no branch is identified with the resident lake fauna or aquatic predators referenced by canon://world/shared-universe-001/ecology/basin-lake-spring-breeding-pulse.

Mana patterns remain open beyond the mass breeder's bounded ordinary tissue-reinforcement case; no Mana organ, specialised ability, System progression, universal creature level, spawn mechanism, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Earth life of any era and mythological creatures may inspire author-facing design; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted directly.
Food, oxygen, minerals, energy, reproduction, disease, injury, mortality, water connectivity, and carrying capacity remain binding ecological constraints.
story_implications: Lake, river, and sea scenes can show a coherent family of flexible bodies, fin-fan control surfaces, and tail propulsion.
The mass breeder reads as one conspicuous, heavily equipped example rather than the lineage norm.
Water connectivity constrains where the lineage can reach, making route geography ecologically load-bearing for it.
Every species, branch, local presence, and encounter requires its own evidence and records.
system_implications: The body plan describes ordinary planetary ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, creature progression rule, spawn source, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: What branches exist, and what fin-fan counts and arrangements do they use?
Which branches carry head shields, ion-exchange organs, or gel chambers, and at what cost?
How do members reproduce outside the mass breeder's mass deposition?
How are freshwater, brackish, and marine ranges divided across the lineage?
Which resident basin-lake fauna, if any, belong to this lineage?
What senses and feeding strategies characterise the lineage's ordinary members?

author_approval.evidence: After the A/B/C ancestral-scope cards were presented with A recommended, the Author selected 'A — Trunk-and-fan core' on 2026-08-17.
